card1.title: Level 1: Spatial Fundamentals and Addition Logic (10 Hours)

card3.title: Level 3: Organic Geometry and Ergonomics (15 Hours)

ent.desc: We teach youth that technology is a means of creation, not just consumption. Through Level 4, students design keychains, custom figures, and accessories, learning to calculate material costs, packaging, and school marketing strategies.

rubric.title: Hybrid Evaluation & Certification System
rubric.subtitle: To obtain Novaforte's official certification at any level, we evaluate both software digital mastery and the physical functionality of the manufactured object.
rubric.digitalDesc: Assessment of CAD design: fully constrained sketches, efficient parametric operations, clean 3D meshes, and optimized slicing parameters.
rubric.physicalDesc: Assessment of the printed part: verification of physical tolerances and clearances (functional assemblies), mechanical strength of layers/infill under impact or traction stress, and surface finish quality.
rubric.badgeDesc: The student must achieve a minimum score of 80% in both components (digital and physical) to receive their official Novaforte Maker Competencies certificate.

curriculum.title: Detailed Curriculum Details
curriculum.subtitle: Click on each level to explore the technical focus, software tools, and suggested practical projects.

level1.title: Level 1: Spatial Fundamentals and Addition Logic (10 Hours)
level1.software: Tinkercad / Tinkercad Classrooms (Intuitive, secure, and free web tool) and introduction to Cura/PrusaSlicer
level1.project: Design a nameplate with raised text, a custom keychain, or a geometric cookie cutter.
level1.learn1: Module 1: The Revolution of Creation. Introduction to additive manufacturing as the art of building by stacking material layer by layer, creating objects without generating waste. Understanding the fundamental workflow: 3D Model, Slicer, and Machine.
level1.learn2: Module 2: The Machine's Brain. Mastery of Slicing software to translate geometries into executable coordinates. Configuration of structural parameters: layer height for resolution, perimeter walls for impact resistance, and gyroid infill patterns to optimize material.
level1.learn3: Module 3: Boolean Logic and Precision. Immersion in the CAD environment (Tinkercad). Use of the Ruler for dimension-guided design and mastery of volumetric subtraction (grouping solids and holes) to sculpt complex geometries.
level1.learn4: Module 4: Digital Architecture. Application of spatial efficiency tools: smart duplication to create repeating patterns (like stairs or basic gears) and manipulation of workplanes to design on inclined surfaces.
level1.learn5: Module 5: Open Ecosystem and Fabrication. Ethical and smart use of open-source repositories and model generation using Artificial Intelligence. Execution of a rigorous digital audit (dimensions, anchors) before exporting the STL file for printing the final project.

level2.title: Level 2: Parametric Design and Functional Mechanics (15 Hours)
level2.software: Onshape (Free industrial-grade CAD web tool for education) or Autodesk Fusion 360
level2.project: Design a mechanical articulated keychain, a phone stand with adjustable angle, or a box with a sliding lid.
level2.learn1: Parametric Sketching: Fundamentals of technical 2D drawing using industrial-grade tools (e.g., Fusion 360 or Onshape). Application of dimensions (exact measurements) and geometric constraints (tangency, parallelism, concentricity) to create stable profiles.
level2.learn2: Volumetric Engineering Operations: Profile extrusion, revolutions for cylindrical parts, and application of technical finishes to dissipate structural stress (chamfers and fillets).
level2.learn3: Tolerance and Mechanism Design: Creation of components with precise clearances (0.2 mm to 0.4 mm) specifically designed to physically fit after thermal contraction of the plastic. Design of simple transmission systems (spur gears, threads).
level2.learn4: Assemblies and Kinematic Simulation: Virtual connection of multiple components using rigid and revolute joints. Verification of movement and collision detection on screen before sending to production.

level3.title: Level 3: Organic Geometry and Ergonomics (15 Hours)
level3.software: Nomad Sculpt (for tablets with stylus) or Blender (professional PC software)
level3.project: Design an articulated fantasy creature, an ergonomic tool housing, or a simplified anatomical/medical model (like a splint or conceptual prosthesis for a pet or human).
level3.learn1: Digital Sculpting and Freeforms: Introduction to subdivision surface modeling (T-Splines or meshes). Using the digital canvas like clay to stretch, flatten, and detail anatomical and fluid geometries.
level3.learn2: Surface Modeling: Advanced modeling techniques (lofts and sweeps) to build ergonomic casings, grips adapted to the human hand, or anatomical supports.
level3.learn3: Reference-Based Design: Importing 2D sketches or X-ray/silhouette photographs into the digital environment to trace and generate 3D models perfectly scaled to real-world proportions.
level3.learn4: Advanced Slicing for Complex Shapes: Configuration of organic supports (tree-type) to protect the surface finish of curved parts, and printing strategies for technical and flexible filaments (TPU, PETG).

level4.title: Level 4: Reverse Engineering and Optimization for Manufacturing (10 Hours)
level4.software: Onshape / Fusion 360 + Advanced Slicers (Bambu Studio / PrusaSlicer)
level4.project: A free project with a social or technological basis, such as automating a simple mechanism or creating a functional prototype for a school enterprise.
level4.learn1: Applied Metrology and Reverse Engineering: Use of the vernier caliper to take exact measurements of damaged commercial parts or physical components. Digital redesign and improvement of the original part.
level4.learn2: Structural Optimization (DfAM): Design rules for 3D printing: elimination of unnecessary supports using self-supporting angles (45-degree rule), bridge design, and model layer orientation to resist maximum mechanical stress.
level4.learn3: Prototype Validation: Basic static stress simulations to identify critical breaking points in the design before fabrication.
level4.learn4: Hybrid Assembly and Post-Processing: Housing design to integrate real hardware and brass heat-set inserts. Finishing the part and presenting the final functional project.

rows.col4: Spatial understanding, basic modeling, and initial slicing.
2D technical drawing, dimensions, constraints, tolerances, and gears.
Digital sculpting, surface modeling, and organic supports.
Caliper usage, DfAM, static validation, and hybrid assembly.
